notes: South-western Cape birds that a visitor to Cape Town and the Western Cape can add to the South Africa trip, hand-picked from the species the country trip does not hold: fynbos and mountain (Victorin's Warbler, Fynbos Buttonquail, Cape Clapper Lark), Overberg fields (Denham's Bustard, White Stork, Lesser Kestrel), Peninsula forest edge and cliffs (three hawks, Peregrine, Booted Eagle, Cape Eagle Owl, Alpine and Common Swift, Common Chaffinch), Cape Flats wetlands (Maccoa Duck, Southern Pochard, Blue-billed Teal, Black-necked Grebe, African Rail, African Snipe, Chestnut-banded Plover, reed warbler, yellow wagtail) and seabirds seen from Cape Point or on a half-day boat trip from Simon's Town or Hout Bay (five albatrosses, petrels, shearwaters, skuas, Sabine's Gull). Most Cape headline birds are already in the country trip (Cape Sugarbird, Orange-breasted Sunbird, Protea Canary, Cape Siskin, Cape Rockjumper, Cape Bulbul, Cape Grassbird, Cape Spurfowl, Blue Crane, African Penguin), so the pack is smaller than the other regions. Left out because another South Africa pack had claimed them when this was written: Lesser Flamingo, White-backed Duck, Squacco and Black-crowned Night Heron, Common, Whiskered, White-winged Black and Little Tern, Terek and Marsh Sandpiper, Common Ringed Plover, Ruddy Turnstone, Red Knot and Eurasian Curlew (all KwaZulu-Natal pack, but just as much West Coast and Langebaan birds), African Dusky Flycatcher and Yellow-bellied Eremomela (KwaZulu-Natal), Southern Tchagra, Mountain Wagtail, Lemon Dove and Olive Woodpecker (Garden Route; all also occur in Cape forests), Layard's Warbler and Southern Penduline Tit (Karoo; both fynbos birds too), Marsh Owl (Lowveld). Ten of this pack's birds were also taken by the Highveld pack after this one was written (see the report). Left out for unreliable photos or ID: Nicholson's Pipit, Plain-backed Pipit, African Swift (flight silhouettes only), Damara Tern (cannot be told from Little Tern in the library), Antarctic Tern. Left out as not a visitor target: Cape Parrot (no usable photos), Knysna and Fynbos-area rarities, vagrant seabirds, royal albatrosses, storm-petrels other than Wilson's. Photos: 24 species with fewer than three approved photos got hand-picked card and quiz photos from contact sheets; the rest use approved photos. Doubtful IDs from photos (seabirds, hawks, buttonquail, owl) are listed in the report.
